questions.title: Pseudoparasite mistaken for a parasite
questions.question: Type of parasite that could be mistaken as parasite during examination?

explanations.A: Incorrect. An obligate parasite is one that cannot live outside a host at all -- a dependency category, not a mistaken-identity artefact.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An incidental parasite is a genuine parasite infecting a host species other than its ordinary one -- it is a real infection, not something mistaken for one.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A facultative parasite can live either freely or parasitically -- again a genuine organism, not an examination artefact.
explanations.D: Correct. A pseudoparasite is any artefact or non-parasitic object -- a plant fibre, a food particle, a free-living mite -- that could be mistaken for a genuine parasite. This mistaken identity happens specifically on microscopic examination of a specimen, when a look-alike structure resembles a true parasitic form. Recognizing pseudoparasites matters clinically, since treating one as a real infection would be an unnecessary intervention.

questions.learning_objective: Identify a pseudoparasite as an artefact mistaken for a genuine parasite during examination.

questions.title: Incidental parasite in a wrong host
questions.question: Type of parasite that establish itself in a host which isn't his ordinary?

explanations.A: Incorrect. An obligate parasite is defined by its inability to live outside a host, not by which host species it infects.
explanations.B: Correct. An incidental (accidental) parasite is one that establishes itself in a host species other than its ordinary one. This is the wrong-host pattern, as when an animal parasite occasionally infects a human who is not its usual host. It is distinct from an erratic parasite, which stays in the correct host but wanders to an abnormal site.
explanations.C: Incorrect. An aberrant (erratic) parasite occurs in the CORRECT host species but wanders to an abnormal body site -- the wrong site, not the wrong host, which is the distinction this stem is testing.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A pseudoparasite is a non-parasitic artefact mistaken for a real parasite, not a genuine parasite in an unusual host.

questions.learning_objective: Identify an incidental (accidental) parasite as one establishing itself in a host species other than its ordinary one.

questions.title: Coprozoic organisms pass through undigested
questions.question: Foreign species that pass through the alimentary tract without infectig the host?

explanations.A: Incorrect. An erratic parasite is a genuine infection that has wandered to an abnormal site within the correct host -- it is not a foreign species passing through undigested.
explanations.B: Correct. A coprozoic organism is a free-living, non-parasitic species from the environment. It passes through the human alimentary tract without infecting the host at any point. It is nonetheless found, still identifiable, in a stool sample, which is why it can be mistaken for a true parasitic finding if not recognized.
explanations.C: Incorrect. An obligate parasite must live inside a host and could not survive as a free-living organism merely transiting the gut.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A facultative parasite can live freely or parasitically, but the stem describes an organism that never infects at all, which is the coprozoic pattern, not the facultative one.

questions.learning_objective: Identify a coprozoic organism as a foreign species passing through the alimentary tract without infecting the host.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 8, p86

questions.title: Erratic parasite in the wrong body site
questions.question: Erratic parasite?

options.A: Establish itself in a host that it is not its ordinary one
options.B: Lives in another place than its normal one of the host
options.C: Can't live outside the host body
options.D: Could be mistaken as a parasite during examination

explanations.A: Incorrect. Establishing itself in a host species other than its ordinary one describes an incidental (accidental) parasite, not an erratic one.
explanations.B: Correct. An erratic (aberrant) parasite occurs in the correct host species. It wanders to a body site, an organ or tissue, other than the one it normally occupies. This is the wrong-site pattern, distinct from an incidental parasite, which is in the correct site but the wrong host species altogether.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Being unable to live outside the host body describes an obligate parasite, a dependency category unrelated to erratic location.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Being mistaken for a parasite during examination describes a pseudoparasite, not a genuine erratic infection.

questions.learning_objective: Identify an erratic (aberrant) parasite as one living in a body site other than its normal one within the correct host.

questions.title: Definitive host harbours the adult stage
questions.question: Host that harbors the adult or sexual stage?

explanations.A: Correct. The definitive (final) host harbours the parasite's adult or sexual reproductive stage. It is the host in which the parasite reaches full maturity. Sexual reproduction, when it occurs in the life cycle, always happens in the definitive host, never in an intermediate or paratenic host.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The intermediate host is where larval developmental stages take place, not the adult/sexual stage.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The paratenic host carries the organism in an arrested state of development, not the mature adult stage.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A transfer host, like a paratenic host, merely carries the organism onward without hosting its adult reproductive stage.

questions.subtopic: Host types in a parasite life cycle
questions.learning_objective: Identify the definitive host as the one harbouring the parasite's adult or sexual stage.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 8, p86

questions.title: Intermediate host: all larval stages
questions.question: In which, all larval stages take place?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The definitive host harbours the adult/sexual stage, reached only after larval development elsewhere.
explanations.B: Correct. The intermediate host is the host in which all of the parasite's larval developmental stages take place. This development continues until the organism becomes infective for the next host in the cycle. Without this stage, the parasite could not reach the form needed to infect its definitive host.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The paratenic host harbours the organism in an arrested state, with no further larval development occurring there.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A transfer host similarly carries the organism without hosting active larval development.

questions.subtopic: Host types in a parasite life cycle
questions.learning_objective: Identify the intermediate host as where all of the parasite's larval stages take place.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 8, p86

questions.title: Reservoir host is a non-human animal harbouring the parasite
questions.question: Another animal than human that harbors the same parasite?

explanations.A: Incorrect. "Definitive host" names a life-cycle role (adult/sexual stage), not the fact of being a non-human animal harbouring the same species.
explanations.B: Incorrect. "Intermediate host" likewise names a developmental role, not the reservoir concept.
explanations.C: Correct. A reservoir host is an animal other than humans that harbours the same parasite species that also infects humans. It need not itself be diseased by the parasite. It serves as an additional source from which humans can become infected, which matters for disease control since eliminating human infection alone would not eliminate the reservoir.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A transfer (paratenic) host carries the organism in arrested development, a different role from being an alternative source-host for human infection.

questions.subtopic: Host types in a parasite life cycle
questions.learning_objective: Identify a reservoir host as a non-human animal harbouring the same parasite that infects humans.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 8, p86

questions.title: Paratenic host: arrested development
questions.question: The host that harbors the organism in an arrested state of development?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The definitive host harbours actively maturing adult/sexual stages, not an arrested one.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The intermediate host is where active larval development happens, the opposite of arrest.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A vector actively transmits the parasite between hosts, often supporting some development, not one where development is specifically arrested.
explanations.D: Correct. The paratenic host harbours the parasite in an arrested state of development. No further maturation occurs there. The host instead simply carries the organism onward until it reaches a host in which development can resume or the definitive host is reached.

questions.subtopic: Host types in a parasite life cycle
questions.learning_objective: Identify the paratenic host as the one harbouring the parasite in an arrested state of development.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 8, p86

questions.title: Transfer host propagates the parasite onward
questions.question: An animal that propagates the parasite carrying it from one place to another?

explanations.A: Incorrect. A vector, typically an arthropod, actively transmits a parasite between hosts, often supporting biological development -- a related but distinct role from simply carrying an organism onward in arrested development.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A reservoir host is an alternative animal source of human infection, not defined by carrying the organism place to place.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "I H" (intermediate host) is where active larval development occurs, not simply onward carriage.
explanations.D: Correct. A transfer (paratenic) host carries the parasite in an arrested state of development. It propagates the organism from one place to another without the parasite maturing further inside it. This continues until the transfer host is eaten by, or otherwise reaches, a host in which development can resume or the definitive host is reached.

questions.subtopic: Host types in a parasite life cycle
questions.learning_objective: Identify the transfer (paratenic) host as the one that carries the parasite onward from place to place.
